messages:

Subject: Solstice + Redwood: initial DPA redlines and SCCs question

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to share our standard DPA redline so legal can review in parallel to MSA/order form finalization. Key asks from our side:

- We prefer the EU Commission SCCs (2021) with the standard modular approach; please confirm Redwood can accept the SCCs as executed between controller and processor.
- We need a short Transfer Impact Addendum for any subprocessors outside the EEA — we attached the template.
- Role clarity: we treat Solstice as controller, Redwood as processor. Please confirm the processor/subprocessor paragraphs align with that.
- Evidence: subprocessor list, SOC2 scope, and retention/export controls — procurement needs these for their security gate.
- Timeline: procurement hopes to sign the order form by 2026-08-13 if legal can get back quickly.

I've attached our redline: Solstice_DPA_redline_v1.docx (see highlights on clauses 4, 7, 9). Can you coordinate with your legal/ops and get an initial response by EOD Wed 2026-08-05?

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a short call if helpful.

Best,
Laura Chen
Head of Legal Ops (Contracts) | Solstice Health
[attachment: Solstice_DPA_redline_v1.docx (docx)]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Solstice + Redwood: initial DPA redlines and SCCs question

Marissa / Ben — forwarding Solstice's redline and asks. Quick summary and my recommendation:

Summary of external asks:
- Adopt EU SCCs (2021) and confirm controller/processor roles
- Add short Transfer Impact Addendum that calls out subprocessors outside EEA
- Provide subprocessor list + SOC2 scope + retention/export control commitments
- Target sign by 2026-08-13

My read: Solstice's redline is mostly standard, they added a few aggressive items on export controls (clauses 7.2/7.3) and a requirement to accept their TIA template with strict assurances about technical measures. I think we can:
- Accept the SCCs but need to map to our subprocessor flow and offer the RI subprocessor list URL (we need to confirm it's up-to-date).
- Push back on any language that converts processor obligations into controller-level warranties (I've flagged a couple of spots).
- For Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA) we can provide a Redwood-drafted TIA that covers our risk assessment approach and commitment to mitigation where feasible; we should decline absolute guarantees on diplomatic/legal outcomes.

Action items for legal/ops:
1) Marissa: take lead on redline markup. Please prioritize clauses: 4 (Data Subject rights/assistance), 7 (International transfers/controls), 9 (Subprocessors).
2) Ben: confirm SOC2 scope and latest subprocessor list URL; export control escalation path and who will sign off on any carveouts.
3) I will propose the timeline to procurement and ask for a quick call if we need to walk through the TIA template.

Target internal deliverable: draft response and our redline to send back to Solstice by 2026-08-05 EOD. If you need more time, tell me by EOD tomorrow so I can reset expectations.

Thanks — Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Fwd: Solstice + Redwood: initial DPA redlines and SCCs question

Thanks for the summary, Soojin. I reviewed Solstice_DPA_redline_v1 and drafted our response (attached RI_response_dpa_comments.docx). High level notes:

1) SCCs: we can accept the 2021 SCCs. We'll incorporate them and map parties in the order form/Annex so it is clear Solstice = controller; Redwood = processor. Suggest we include a brief Annex A that lists purpose and categories of personal data to avoid future confusion.

2) Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA): we will NOT sign their template as-is. Their TIA contains language asking us to guarantee impact mitigations across third-country jurisdictions — this is not feasible. I drafted a Redwood TIA that:
   - explains our assessment approach (technical and contractual mitigations),
   - commits to reasonable cooperation to remediate if a legal risk materializes,
   - sets expectations that ultimate legal risk often depends on destination jurisdiction and local authorities.

3) Subprocessors and evidence: we should provide a current subprocessor list URL plus a SOC 2 summary PDF. Ben, please confirm exact SOC2 report name and an export-safe link. If SOC2 report is under NDA, we'll offer an executive summary + SOC2 Type II date and auditor.

4) Export controls / warranties (clauses 7.x): push back on absolute warranties. Proposed language: "Redwood will use commercially reasonable technical and organizational measures to prevent unauthorized export of covered personal data and will cooperate with Customer on reasonably available mitigations."

5) Timeline: We can deliver our redline and supporting artifacts by EOD 2026-08-05. However, we need procurement to confirm internal sign-off path (legal + security + procurement) by 2026-08-11 to hit their 2026-08-13 signature target. If procurement cannot commit, we should request a short extension.

Attached: RI_response_dpa_comments.docx (contains clause-by-clause redline and suggested alternative language), Transfer_Impact_Addendum_Draft.pdf (Redwood TIA draft).

I'll mark the document for the three hot spots above. Ben — when you confirm the SOC2 link and subprocessor URL, I will insert references in the redline and finalize.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

Subject: Solstice — Redwood redline + TIA draft and next steps

Hi Laura / Procurement team,

Thanks for the redline. Attached are two documents:
- RI_response_dpa_comments.docx — clause-by-clause redline and proposed language
- Transfer_Impact_Addendum_Draft.pdf — Redwood's proposed TIA that explains our assessment approach and cooperation commitments.

Short summary of our positions:
- SCCs: we will adopt the EU 2021 SCCs and will include the executed SCC Annexes pointing at the Order Form.
- Controller/processor mapping: confirmed — Solstice = controller; Redwood = processor. We'll add an Annex A (data schema / categories) in the Order Form.
- Subprocessors: we will provide the current public subprocessor list and SOC2 summary. Ben will follow up with the exact links.
- TIA: we cannot accept absolute remedial guarantees. Our TIA provides a clear mitigation and escalation flow.
- Export control language: we've softened the warranty language to commercially reasonable measures and cooperative remediation.

Requested next steps from Solstice:
1) Review our redline and the TIA draft (attached) and flag any non-starters within 48 hours.
2) Confirm the internal approval chain + any additional security evidence required (specific SOC2 items or penetration test reports).
3) If everything is acceptable, please confirm you want DocuSign execution and the contact for signature (name + email).

We are aiming to have a clean order form + DPA ready to go to signature by 2026-08-13. If Solstice needs a short extension, let us know — we can be flexible by a few business days.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
